comments.content: `recipientID` breaks the naming convention used everywhere else in this file (`userId` on the `album.invite` event) and in the album-invite job type (`recipientId` in `INotifyAlbumInviteJob`). Renaming now (before merge) keeps the event payloads consistent; otherwise every consumer has to remember the odd capitalization.

The tolerant error handling was dropped here. `Job.remove()` throws `Missing key for job ...` when the job disappears between `getJob()` and `remove()` (concurrent API workers, job already completed/auto-removed). `removeJob` is awaited inside `NotificationService.onAlbumUpdate`, which is invoked by the event emitter without a try/catch, so such a race would now reject the event handler and the fresh delayed notification job would never be queued. Keep swallowing the "missing key" case.

The composite job id (`<albumId>/<recipientId>`) is now a contract shared with `NotificationService.onAlbumUpdate`, which rebuilds the exact same string to call `removeJob(JobName.NOTIFY_ALBUM_UPDATE, `${id}/${recipientID}`)`. Two hand-written constructions must stay byte-identical; if only one changes, removal silently misses the job and delayed album-update emails are no longer collapsed per recipient. Extract the id builder into a single exported helper used by both call sites.

The deprecation note is inaccurate and contradicts the new usage. The only caller of `removeJob` after this change is `NotificationService.onAlbumUpdate` (album notifications) — asset notifications never used it (previously it was only used to merge pending album-update jobs). Marking a method as deprecated in the same change that makes it a load-bearing part of the album-notification flow is confusing, and a plain `// deprecated` comment does not surface in IDEs. Either drop the note, or use a proper JSDoc tag with an accurate reason.

comments.content: The removed implementation filtered recipients through `album.albumUsers` + `owner`, so a recipient that had been removed from the album before the delayed job fired would not receive an email. The new code only checks that the user still exists, so a user removed from the album within the 5-minute delay window will still receive an email containing the album name and thumbnail. Since the album (with `albumUsers`) is already loaded here, please re-validate membership before sending.

Each `emit('album.update', ...)` now independently enqueues/removes a notification job, and they are awaited sequentially inside the loop. This makes `addAssets` latency grow linearly with album membership (2 Redis round trips per member) and, because `EventRepository.emit` awaits handlers sequentially and lets listener errors propagate, a failure for one recipient aborts the remaining emits and fails the whole request after the assets were already added. Prefer firing them concurrently so every recipient is attempted.

Naming is inconsistent with the neighboring `INotifyAlbumInviteJob.recipientId` (and `JobName.NOTIFY_ALBUM_INVITE` payloads) which use the `Id` suffix. Using `recipientID` for the same concept in the same job map makes the payload shapes easy to mix up; consider renaming to `recipientId` for consistency.

Two leftovers from the recipients-loop removal in this handler:
1. `owner` is now fetched only for an existence check (`album.ownerId` is no longer used to build the recipient list), so that extra `userRepository.get` is dead work that now runs once per recipient job.
2. The thumbnail attachment query and `getConfig({ withCache: false })` are executed before we know whether this recipient actually needs an email. Since the job is now per-recipient, this work is repeated for every album member even when the user is gone or has `albumUpdate` notifications disabled.

Suggest dropping the `owner` lookup and moving the user/preference checks above `getAlbumThumbnailAttachment`/`getConfig` (the same order `handleAlbumInvite` uses).

comments.content: The job id format `${id}/${recipientID}` is duplicated here and in `JobRepository.getJobOptions()` (`jobId: `${item.data.id}/${item.data.recipientID}``). If one of the two formats is changed later, `removeJob` silently no-ops (it swallows missing jobs), so the 5-minute debounce reset would stop working without any error. Consider extracting the id construction into one shared helper/constant (e.g. `getAlbumUpdateJobId(id, recipientId)`) used by both places.
